angle: skip the 8-row odds table: show one flip stream and ask what came right before the first heads-heads-heads; the answer is tails, so tails-heads-heads got there one flip earlier, and the 7 in 8 drops out of the picture. Then the one-line rule that beats any choice, and a checkable question (what beats HTH?)
title: Pick any 3 coin flips. I can pick 3 that beat yours
description:
Pick heads, heads, heads. We flip a coin until one of our sequences shows up, and I pick tails, heads, heads: I win 7 times in 8. The first time heads-heads-heads appears, the flip just before it must be tails (or it would have appeared one flip earlier), so tails-heads-heads always got there first, unless the game opens with three heads. That is Penney's game (Walter Penney, 1969).

The rule works against every choice: flip your middle coin, put it in front, drop your last. It wins at least 2 times in 3 against all 8 sequences. Checked with exact fractions for all 8 sequences and by simulating 200,000 games (THH won 87.4%, against an exact 87.5%).
facts_checked: each run of 3 flips has chance 1/8; there are 8 runs
THH appears before HHH with probability exactly 7/8 = 87.5% (Conway's leading numbers, exact fractions)
HHH wins only if the first three flips are HHH: 1/8
rule 'flip the middle, put it in front, drop the last' answers HHH with THH and HTH with HHT
the rule wins at least 2/3 against all 8 sequences (7/8, 3/4, 2/3, 2/3, 2/3, 2/3, 3/4, 7/8)
HHT beats HTH 2/3 (answer to the closing question)
simulation: 200,000 games THH vs HHH, THH won 87.4%; 100,000 games HHT vs HTH, HHT won 66.5%
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penney%27s_game (Walter Penney, Journal of Recreational Mathematics, 1969; table of best responses)

beats.say: Pick heads, heads, heads, and I'll pick three flips that beat it 7 times in 8.
That sounds impossible. Every run of three flips is equally likely. One in 8 each.
Here's the game. We flip a coin until one of our sequences shows up. Whoever's appears first wins.
You picked heads, heads, heads. I pick tails, heads, heads.
Look at the first time heads, heads, heads appears. What came right before it?
It has to be tails. If it were heads, you'd have had three heads one flip earlier.
And tails, heads, heads is my sequence. It was already there, one flip ahead of you.
So you only win if the first three flips are all heads. That's one in 8. I win the other 7.
It works against anything. Flip your middle coin, put it in front, drop your last. I win at least 2 times in 3.
There's a new one of these every day. Your turn: you pick heads, tails, heads. What should I pick?
